title: Ordinary derived tensor comparison under compatible coefficient isomorphisms
statement: Let R0,A0,B0,C0 and R,A,B,C be commutative rings of one universe, with the two base algebra diagrams and tensor-algebra maps to C0 and C. Choose possibly different derived-category morphism universes for the two diagrams [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let Q0 and Q be input complexes and M,N their base-derived tensor cohomology models [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Given compatible eR,eA,eB and an A0-linear chain isomorphism q from Q0 to restriction of Q along eA, in every degree i there exist a tensor-ring equivalence eE sending a tensor b to eA(a) tensor eB(b), a chain isomorphism s of the ordinary tensor complexes semilinear along eE and sending r tensor x to eE(r) tensor q(x), and an eE-semilinear cohomology isomorphism k. The square k;restriction(N.comparison);inverse exact restriction homology factor equals M.comparison;homology(s). The conclusion uses no maps to C0 or C, no ordinaryToLocalized or localizedComparison, and no flatness assumption.

source.place: Lemma 15.61.1, independence of choices and universal derived change of rings; coefficient-equivalence and two-universe refinement of the item ordinary-comparison plan.

proof.text: Construct forward and inverse tensor-ring maps with Algebra.TensorProduct.mapRingHom, using compatibility and its inverse. Tensor induction and mapRingHom_tmul prove both inverse laws; this yields eE with the prescribed pure-tensor formula.

For any compatible scalar ring equivalences, construct termwise scalar-extension isomorphisms using semilinear LinearEquiv structures and TensorProduct.congr. Tensor induction proves linearity for the target coefficient ring. In each degree use q's component; test the differential square on 1 tensor x via ExtendScalars.hom_ext. The generator formula and q.hom.comm close it. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents assembles s.
Apply lem-pc-base-derived-tensor-restricted-ring-comparison to the eE and s just constructed. It supplies kB, its compatibility with a tensor 1, and the underlying ordinary comparison square.

Take the additive equivalence underlying kB. Its B0-linearity gives compatibility with 1 tensor b. Write a tensor b as (a tensor 1)(1 tensor b); multiplication of scalar actions and the two compatibilities give eE-semilinearity on pure tensors. Zero and addition cases finish tensor induction. LinearEquiv.ofBijective with the restricted target action makes it an E0-linear equivalence, hence the desired ModuleCat isomorphism k. Extensionality turns the pointwise comparison identity into the required morphism equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_baseDerivedTensor_ordinary_ring_comparison
    {R₀ A₀ B₀ C₀ R A B C : Type u}
    [CommRing R₀] [CommRing A₀] [CommRing B₀] [CommRing C₀]
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra R₀ A₀] [Algebra R₀ B₀] [Algebra (A₀ ⊗[R₀] B₀) C₀]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra (A ⊗[R] B) C]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R₀)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} B₀)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (Q₀ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A₀) ℤ)
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (M : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R₀ A₀ B₀ Q₀ C₀)
    (N : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q C)
    (eR : R₀ ≃+* R) (eA : A₀ ≃+* A) (eB : B₀ ≃+* B)
    (hRA : eA.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R₀ A₀) =
      (algebraMap R A).comp eR.toRingHom)
    (hRB : eB.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R₀ B₀) =
      (algebraMap R B).comp eR.toRingHom)
    (q : Q₀ ≅ ((restrictScalars.{u} eA.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q)
    (i : ℤ) :
    let K₀ := ((extendScalars (algebraMap A₀ (A₀ ⊗[R₀] B₀))).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj Q₀
    let K := ((extendScalars (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B))).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj Q
    ∃ (eE : (A₀ ⊗[R₀] B₀) ≃+* (A ⊗[R] B)),
      (∀ (a : A₀) (b : B₀), eE (a ⊗ₜ[R₀] b) = eA a ⊗ₜ[R] eB b) ∧
      ∃ (s : K₀ ≅ ((restrictScalars.{u} eE.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj K)
        (k : M.cohomology i ≅ (restrictScalars.{u} eE.toRingHom).obj (N.cohomology i)),
        (∀ (j : ℤ) (r : A₀ ⊗[R₀] B₀) (x : Q₀.X j),
          s.hom.f j (r ⊗ₜ[A₀, algebraMap A₀ (A₀ ⊗[R₀] B₀)] x) =
            eE r ⊗ₜ[A, algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)] (show Q.X j from q.hom.f j x)) ∧
        k.hom ≫ (restrictScalars.{u} eE.toRingHom).map (N.comparison i) ≫
            ((K.sc i).mapHomologyIso (restrictScalars.{u} eE.toRingHom)).inv =
          M.comparison i ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap s.hom i
